stem: By Sikh tradition, who wrote out the Adi Granth as its scribe while Guru Arjan compiled it in 1604?
options: Baba Buddha
Bhai Mani Singh
Bhai Gurdas
Bhai Nand Lal
why: Tradition holds that Guru Arjan dictated and Bhai Gurdas wrote out the Adi Granth, installed at Harmandir Sahib in 1604; Baba Buddha became its first granthi.
source: Sikh tradition on the compilation of the Adi Granth (1604)

es.stem: Según la tradición sij, ¿quién escribió como escriba el Adi Granth mientras Gurú Arjan lo compilaba en 1604?
options: Baba Buddha
Bhai Mani Singh
Bhai Gurdas
Bhai Nand Lal
es.why: La tradición dice que Gurú Arjan dictó y Bhai Gurdas escribió el Adi Granth, instalado en Harmandir Sahib en 1604; Baba Buddha fue su primer granthi.

stem: Besides Gurbani, the Sikh Rehat Maryada allows kirtan in the congregation from the works of which two poets?
options: Bhai Gurdas and Bhai Nand Lal
Bhai Mani Singh and Bhai Gurdas
Bhai Nand Lal and Bhai Mani Singh
Bhai Santokh Singh and Bhai Gurdas
why: The Sikh Rehat Maryada's section on kirtan says only Gurbani may be sung in the sangat, along with its explanation in the compositions of Bhai Gurdas and Bhai Nand Lal.
source: Sikh Rehat Maryada, chapter on kirtan

es.stem: Además del Gurbani, el Sikh Rehat Maryada permite el kirtan en la congregación con las obras de ¿cuáles dos poetas?
options: Bhai Gurdas y Bhai Nand Lal
Bhai Mani Singh y Bhai Gurdas
Bhai Nand Lal y Bhai Mani Singh
Bhai Santokh Singh y Bhai Gurdas
es.why: La sección sobre el kirtan del Sikh Rehat Maryada dice que en la sangat solo se canta el Gurbani, junto con su explicación en las obras de Bhai Gurdas y Bhai Nand Lal.

stem: In the sakhi of Guru Nanak at Multan, the city's holy men send him a cup brimming with milk. What does his floating a jasmine flower on it say?
options: he will leave Multan without entering the city
he will stay lightly, adding fragrance, crowding no one
he claims the city's holy seat for his own teaching
he returns their gift to show he needs nothing at all
why: The full cup said Multan was already full of holy men; the jasmine resting on top without spilling it answered that Nanak would add fragrance and displace no one. Janamsakhi tradition.
source: Janamsakhi tradition, Guru Nanak at Multan

es.stem: En la sakhi de Gurú Nanak en Multán, los santones de la ciudad le envían una taza llena de leche hasta el borde. ¿Qué dice él al hacer flotar una flor de jazmín encima?
options: que se irá de Multán sin entrar en la ciudad
que se quedará con ligereza, dando aroma, sin desplazar a nadie
que reclama el asiento santo de la ciudad para su enseñanza
que les devuelve el regalo para mostrar que no necesita nada
es.why: La taza llena decía que Multán ya estaba llena de santones; el jazmín flotando sin derramarla respondía que Nanak daría aroma sin desplazar a nadie. Tradición de las janamsakhis.

stem: In the Sikh story of the cowherd boy who became Baba Buddha, why does Guru Nanak call him 'buddha', the old one?
options: he was the eldest of Nanak's first circle of disciples
he had been born, the story says, with white hair
he was chosen as headman of his village council
he saw that death takes the young as well as the old
why: The boy told Nanak that small sticks catch fire before big logs, so death does not wait for the old; Nanak said he spoke like an old man and called him Buddha.
source: Sikh tradition on Baba Buddha's meeting with Guru Nanak

es.stem: En la historia sij del niño pastor que llegó a ser Baba Buddha, ¿por qué Gurú Nanak lo llama 'buddha', el viejo?
options: era el mayor del primer círculo de discípulos de Nanak
según la historia, había nacido con el pelo blanco
lo eligieron jefe del consejo de su aldea
vio que la muerte se lleva a jóvenes y viejos por igual
es.why: El niño le dijo a Nanak que las ramitas arden antes que los troncos grandes, así que la muerte no espera a los viejos; Nanak dijo que hablaba como un anciano y lo llamó Buddha.

stem: In his hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib, Kabir leaves Kashi to die at Maghar. What point does that move make?
options: Maghar was the town where his teacher Ramanand lived
the rulers of Kashi had banished him from their city
release comes from the Lord, not where one dies
he wished to be buried among his weaver kinsfolk
why: Kashi was held to grant liberation to those who died there and Maghar the opposite; Kabir asks what he would owe the Lord if he were freed just by dying in Kashi. Kabir, Raag Gauri, Ang 326.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Gauri, Kabir, Ang 326

es.stem: En sus himnos del Gurú Granth Sahib, Kabir deja Kashi para morir en Maghar. ¿Qué quiere mostrar con eso?
options: Maghar era el pueblo donde vivía su maestro Ramanand
los gobernantes de Kashi lo habían desterrado
la liberación viene del Señor, no de dónde se muere
quería ser enterrado entre sus parientes tejedores
es.why: Se creía que morir en Kashi daba la liberación y morir en Maghar lo contrario; Kabir pregunta qué le debería al Señor si se liberara solo por morir en Kashi. Kabir, Raag Gauri, Ang 326.

stem: Farid's salok on Ang 1378 says not to write black marks against others. A friend keeps a running list of a coworker's faults. Where would that salok turn the friend?
options: to taking the list to an elder to judge it fairly
to praying each day that the coworker will change
to forgiving the faults but keeping the list safe
to looking at the faults under their own collar
why: Farid says: if you are wise and subtle, do not write black marks against others; bow your head and look under your own collar. Guru Granth Sahib, Salok Farid, Ang 1378.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Salok Sheikh Farid, Ang 1378

es.stem: El salok de Farid en el Ang 1378 dice que no escribas marcas negras contra otros. Un amigo lleva una lista de las faltas de un compañero de trabajo. ¿Hacia dónde lo dirigiría ese salok?
options: a llevar la lista a un mayor para que la juzgue
a orar cada día para que el compañero cambie
a perdonar las faltas pero guardar la lista
a mirar las faltas bajo su propio cuello
es.why: Farid dice: si eres sabio y sutil, no escribas marcas negras contra otros; inclina la cabeza y mira bajo tu propio cuello. Gurú Granth Sahib, Salok de Farid, Ang 1378.

stem: In Namdev's hymn in Raag Malar (Ang 1292), what happens to him at the temple, and how does the hymn end?
why: Namdev says he came laughing to the temple, was seized and thrown out for his low caste as a cloth-printer, and sat behind it; as he sang the Lord's praises, the temple turned to face him. Raag Malar, Namdev, Ang 1292.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Malar, Namdev, Ang 1292

rubric.point: Says he is thrown out or turned away because of his low caste or birth (a cloth-printer). 'He was not allowed in' with no reason counts as partly.
Says the temple turns around to face him while he sings the Lord's praises from behind it. 'God came to him' without the temple turning counts as partly.
Mentions that he keeps singing rather than fighting, or that the hymn shows the Lord honoring the low-born devotee (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el himno de Namdev en Raag Malar (Ang 1292), ¿qué le pasa en el templo y cómo termina el himno?
es.why: Namdev cuenta que llegó riendo al templo, lo agarraron y lo echaron por su casta baja de estampador de telas, y se sentó detrás; mientras cantaba las alabanzas del Señor, el templo giró para mirarlo de frente. Raag Malar, Namdev, Ang 1292.

stem: The Guru Granth Sahib holds hymns by bhagats such as Kabir, Sheikh Farid, Namdev and Ravidas beside the Gurus' own. Why are they there, and how are they treated?
why: Guru Arjan included bhagats of many backgrounds, Hindu and Muslim, high- and low-born, whose hymns share the Gurus' message of the One and the Name; their words are part of the Guru and are read and sung with the same reverence. Adi Granth, 1604.
source: Guru Granth Sahib (Adi Granth compiled by Guru Arjan, 1604)

rubric.point: Says their hymns share the Gurus' message, such as devotion to the One or the Name, or rejection of caste and empty ritual. 'They were holy men' alone counts as partly.
Says their hymns are revered and sung like the Gurus' own, as part of the Guru, not as lesser additions.
Mentions that Guru Arjan compiled them in 1604, or that the bhagats came from different castes and from Hindu and Muslim backgrounds (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: El Gurú Granth Sahib reúne himnos de bhagats como Kabir, el jeque Farid, Namdev y Ravidas junto a los de los Gurús. ¿Por qué están ahí y cómo se los trata?
es.why: Gurú Arjan incluyó bhagats de muchos orígenes, hindúes y musulmanes, de casta alta y baja, cuyos himnos comparten el mensaje de los Gurús sobre el Uno y el Nombre; sus palabras son parte del Gurú y se leen y cantan con la misma reverencia. Adi Granth, 1604.
